entries.description: to Pythagoras has hardly any claim to be regarded as authentic
entries.subject: to Pythagoras
entries.object: hardly any claim to be regarded as authentic

spans.text: The tradition which assigns the first employment of the Greek word φιλοσοφία to Pythagoras has hardly any claim to be regarded as authentic; and the somewhat self-conscious modesty to which Diogenes Laërtius attributes the choice of the designation is, in all probability, a piece of etymology crystallized into narrative.

entries.description: The same thought is to be found in Xenophon
entries.subject: The same
entries.object: is to be found in Xenophon

spans.text: The same thought is to be found in Xenophon, and is doubtless to be attributed to the historical Socrates.

entries.description: the Socratic doctrine that virtue is knowledge
entries.subject: the Socratic

spans.text: In Socrates and Plato, on the other hand, the start is made from a consideration of man’s moral and intellectual activity; but knowledge and action are confused with one another, as in the Socratic doctrine that virtue is knowledge.

entries.task_id: but there|has|since been appropriated to it
entries.description: but there has since been appropriated to it
entries.subject: but there

spans.text: For this investigation Aristotle’s most usual name is “first philosophy” or, as a modern might say, “first principles”; but there has since been appropriated to it, apparently by accident, the title “metaphysics.”
It has frequently tended, however, and still tends, to be used as specially convertible with the narrower term “metaphysics.”

entries.task_id: art of|thought|or a doctrine of fallacies
entries.description: art of thought or a doctrine of fallacies
entries.subject: art of

spans.text: Similarly, logic, so far as it is an art of thought or a doctrine of fallacies, and ethics, so far as it is occupied with a natural history of impulses and moral sentiments, do neither of them belong, except by courtesy, to the philosophic province.
